title: The Statue of Liberty
subtitle: A present from France, a long trip in 214 boxes, and the first thing new Americans saw.
description: An A1 reading and listening text on the Statue of Liberty: where it came from, how it arrived, and what it meant to people on the ships.
source: authored for this site; no source document
passage: In New York, a green woman stands in the water. She is forty-six meters tall. In her right hand she has a light.
The statue is a present. It is a present from France to the United States.
A French artist, Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi, made it. People in France paid for the statue. People in the United States paid for the big stone under it.
In 1885 the statue came to New York in a ship, in 214 big boxes. Workers built it on a small island. It opened in October 1886.
The statue is green now, but it was brown at first. It is made of copper, and copper changes color in the rain and the wind. This takes about thirty years.
After 1892, ships with new people from Europe arrived next to the island. The statue was the first big thing they saw in America.
Many of these people were poor. They were tired after two or three weeks on the sea. Some of them cried.
There are words on the statue, from a poem by Emma Lazarus: “Give me your tired, your poor...”
Today you can take a boat to the island. You can go inside the statue and look at New York from her head.
More than four million people visit her every year. She is not only a statue now. For many people, she is a word: welcome.

exercises.title: True or False?
exercises.instructions: Decide if each sentence is true or false.

items.statement: The statue was green at the beginning.
items.explanation: False — it was brown. The copper changed colour over about thirty years.

items.statement: The statue is on an island.
items.explanation: True — workers built it on a small island in the water.

items.statement: People in the United States paid for everything.
items.explanation: False — people in France paid for the statue; people in the United States paid for the stone under it.

items.statement: You can go inside the statue today.
items.explanation: True — you can go inside and look at New York from her head.
